note: Phase 14, a recorded divergence: Emacs' nil is an ordinary symbol and carries a property list like any other, so `(put nil 'a 1)` stores. fe's nil is a distinct object type with no storage of its own, so `put` refuses it by name -- `(wrong-type-argument symbolp nil)` -- rather than accepting the write and dropping it. The reading side agrees: `(get nil 'a)` is nil in fe, which is also what Emacs answers before anything was put.
